business_scope.primary_industry_name: Non-Dilutive Revenue-Based Financing for Digital Brands

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Cayman Islands Companies Act (As Revised, 2021 Revision), Part II (ss. 12-14) for incorporation, s. 97 and Part X on Exempted Companies; for any physical UK presence, UK Companies Act 2006, Part 34 (ss. 1043-1059) on registration of overseas companies
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cayman Islands Registrar of Companies, General Registry (Grand Cayman); UK Companies House for Part 34 overseas/establishment registration
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association (M&A) filed through the Registrar's eServices portal; UK Form OS1 where a UK establishment is registered
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum issued or paid-up share capital; one subscriber share of no par value is generally allotted (often US$1). No escrow account or capital deposit is required by the Cayman Registrar, and UK Part 34 registration imposes no minimum capitalization.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: (1) the subscription for one ordinary share of no par value by the sole subscriber be and is hereby accepted and allotted fully paid against the recorded consideration; (2) the registered office of the Company be and is hereby fixed at the address maintained by the registered office provider, which is authorized to accept service of process; (3) the persons named in Schedule A be and they are hereby appointed as first directors, to hold office until changed by ordinary resolution; (4) the corporate secretary named in Schedule B is hereby appointed; and (5) any director be empowered to execute banking forms, lease agreements, and statutory filings to give effect to these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Entity Type Confirmation and Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cayman Islands General Registry – Registrar of Companies (eServices portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the vehicle is an exempted company limited by shares; file a name reservation request; verify the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name and includes 'Limited' or 'Ltd.'; receive the reserved name certificate valid for 90 days.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, submit an alternative name or file a written appeal to the Registrar with supporting justification; reserve a new name without additional penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cayman Islands General Registry (filing); execution before the registered office provider and notarization where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association providing for exempted status, no par value share capital, and objects covering royalty financing and revenue-based financing; execute the M&A by the sole subscriber; have signatures notarized or certified as required for later UK Companies House or bank onboarding.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar identifies deficiencies in the M&A, amend and re-submit the revised documents within 15 business days; the registry will issue a query notice specifying the corrective action.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Incorporation Filing and Fee Payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cayman Islands Registrar of Companies, General Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed M&A together with the application for incorporation and declaration of compliance via the eServices portal; pay the government registration fee (approximately US$850 plus filing charges); obtain the Certificate of Incorporation upon successful registration.
required_dossiers: Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected, cure the stated deficiencies within 21 days and re-submit; an expedited review is available for an additional government fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Officer Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors; records maintained at the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting; adopt board resolutions allotting the initial subscriber share, fixing the registered office, appointing the first directors and corporate secretary; issue share certificates; complete statutory registers of members, directors, and charges.
required_dossiers: Consent-to-act forms from each director and secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a proposed officer declines appointment, execute a deed of appointment for a substitute and update the registers within 14 days; no registry filing is required for the internal appointment itself.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: UK Establishment Registration as Overseas Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: UK Companies House – Overseas Company Registration Unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the exempted company establishes a physical or administrative presence in Great Britain, register under Part 34 of the Companies Act 2006: complete Form OS1 with particulars of the establishment, a certified English translation of constitutional documents, and a certified copy of the Certificate of Incorporation; pay the £40 fee and receive the UK establishment registration number.
required_dossiers: Apostilled certified copy of Cayman Certificate of Incorporation
Certified copy of M&A with English translation
UK registered office or memorandum address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Companies House may reject inconsistent particulars; correct and resubmit within 28 days; late or defective registration is subject to penalties under s. 1047 of the Companies Act 2006.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cayman Islands Monetary Authority (CIMA) – AML/CFT Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Assess whether the revenue-based financing activity constitutes 'relevant financial business' under the Anti-Money Laundering Regulations (2022 Revision); if in scope, submit the AML registration through CIMA's Regulatory Enhanced Electronic Submission System; appoint an AML Compliance Officer, Money Laundering Reporting Officer, and Deputy MLRO; adopt AML/CFT policies and a risk-based customer due diligence framework.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIMA issues a compliance deficiency notice, file a remediation response within 30 days; repeated non-compliance may attract civil penalties, so any material change in activity must be notified promptly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Economic Substance and Annual Statutory Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cayman Islands Tax Information Authority (TIA) and General Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Economic Substance Notification and, where the activity falls within 'financing and leasing' or 'pure equity holding', submit the Economic Substance Return confirming adequate substance and tax residence; file the annual return and declaration to the Registrar and pay the annual government fee to maintain good standing.
required_dossiers: Audited or unaudited financial statements (if required)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late filings attract fines under the Economic Substance Law and Companies Act; apply to the TIA or Registrar for an extension with reasonable cause before the statutory deadline and settle any penalty promptly.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial licensing board applies to an office-based financing entity; the relevant oversight authority is the Cayman Islands Monetary Authority (AML/CFT Division) for financial-crime registration and the Cayman Islands Department of Environment for premises-related environmental compliance only.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sectoral operating license required; optional AML/CFT Registration as a Relevant Financial Business under the Anti-Money Laundering Regulations (2022 Revision) where the revenue-based financing activity is deemed in scope.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Cayman Islands Department of Environment (DoE); UK Environment Agency if a physical UK office is established
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – administrative, office-only activity with no industrial discharges, no manufacturing process, and no generation of regulated emissions
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source wastewater or VOC emissions; office waste handled under the Waste Management Regulations; UK branch reporting aligned with Streamlined Energy and Carbon Reporting (SECR) thresholds where applicable; no EIA screening required.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification per the Cayman Islands Fire Services Act for the registered-office premises; structural load inspection certificate for leased office space; in the UK, workplace clearance and health-and-safety compliance under the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 with a fire risk assessment and employer liability cover.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Her Majesty's Revenue and Customs (HMRC); official portal: GOV.UK online services for Corporation Tax, VAT, PAYE and Customs Declaration Service; Companies House for the registration of UK establishments of foreign companies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Determine UK tax residence. The Cayman Exempted Company is not automatically UK-resident but becomes UK-resident if its central management and control is exercised in the UK. Step 2: If UK-resident, register for Corporation Tax via HMRC online services or by letter using form CT41G and obtain a Unique Taxpayer Reference (UTR). Step 3: If the company is non-UK resident but carries on a trade in the UK through a UK permanent establishment (PE), register for Corporation Tax with HMRC and obtain a UTR; if non-UK resident and no UK PE, no UK Corporation Tax registration is required, but UK-source income may still be within the charge if statutory gateway applies. Step 4: If the company is a non-established taxable person making taxable supplies in the UK, apply for UK VAT registration using HMRC form VAT2 through the Non-Established Taxable Persons Unit and obtain a UK VAT Registration Number (VRN). Step 5: For goods movements, apply to HMRC for a GB EORI number via GOV.UK to make customs declarations. Step 6: If the company has UK employees, register as an employer for PAYE and National Insurance. Step 7: If the foreign company establishes a registered UK establishment under Part 34 of the Companies Act 2006, register that establishment at Companies House and obtain a UK establishment registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The UK does not provide a check-the-box or elective entity classification regime. A Cayman Exempted Company is always treated as a separate corporate entity for UK tax purposes and cannot elect pass-through treatment. If central management and control is exercised in the UK, the company is UK-resident and taxed on worldwide profits at entity level; if non-resident, only UK-source income and PE-attributable profits are charged. Hybrid mismatch counteractions under TIOPA 2010 Part 6A apply automatically and no election is available. A non-established business may appoint a fiscal representative for VAT under VATA 1994 s48, but that is an administrative arrangement and does not alter entity classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Value Added Tax Act 1994
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GBP 90,000 annual taxable turnover for UK-established businesses; non-established taxable persons are required to register for VAT if they make any taxable supply in the UK, without applying the GBP 90,000 threshold. Distance selling and e-commerce OSS thresholds apply separately where relevant.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The UK does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance or mandatory digital stamping system. VAT-registered businesses must comply with Making Tax Digital for VAT, meaning digital records must be kept and VAT returns must be submitted through HMRC-recognised software via the HMRC Application Programming Interface (API). E-invoicing is accepted; pre-clearance of invoices is not required. Customs import and export declarations must be submitted electronically through the Customs Declaration Service (CDS).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: export zero-rating is available under VATA 1994 Schedule 8 where goods are exported from the UK to a destination outside the UK, are directly removed from the UK, and the supplier holds prescribed official and commercial evidence of export within the relevant time limits. Offshore services: supplies made to a recipient belonging outside the UK are generally outside the scope of UK VAT by place-of-supply rules; specified services may be zero-rated under Schedule 8 if the statutory conditions are satisfied. For this royalty financing fund, pure financing and revenue-based financing supplies are typically VAT-exempt or outside the scope of UK VAT rather than zero-rated; evidence of the non-UK recipient and the export-linked financing arrangement must be maintained.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: HMRC may deny zero-rating, assess VAT and recover interest if the required customs and remittance evidence is unavailable, if invoicing or payment flows are inconsistent with a genuine export, or if the 180-day repatriation evidence deadline is missed. Civil penalties range from 30% to 100% of the avoided VAT, increased for deliberate concealment and mitigated only by prompt and unprompted disclosure. Fraudulent evasion of VAT is a criminal offence under VATA 1994 s72, punishable by up to 7 years imprisonment and unlimited fines; customs misuse may also trigger liability under CEMA 1979.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of England (central bank for the United Kingdom); in the Cayman Islands, the Cayman Islands Monetary Authority administers the currency board. HM Treasury retains ultimate financial sanctions and anti-money laundering oversight. No dedicated UK foreign exchange control administration exists.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Pound Sterling is fully convertible with no exchange controls on current account or capital account transactions; profit remittances, dividends, and royalty payments from the United Kingdom are unrestricted and subject only to standard corporate tax withholding or reporting obligations. The Cayman Islands imposes no exchange controls, and the Cayman Islands Dollar is pegged to the US Dollar at a fixed rate of 0.8333 KYD per 1.00 USD; conversion of KYD to other currencies is freely permitted. For a Cayman exempted company holding funds in UK banks, there are no restrictions on transferring capital, debt service, or profits out of the UK.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: United Kingdom: no statutory timeline exists for surrendering export proceeds, and there is no mandatory conversion ratio; exporters may retain and freely deploy foreign currency receipts. Cayman Islands: no exchange control regime and no export proceeds surrender requirement; all export receipts may be retained in any currency, banked freely, and invested without prior central bank consent.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderately viable for an FCA-regulated electronic money institution licensed in the UK, such as Mercuryo, Revolut Business, or Paysafe, which may onboard a Cayman exempted company through enhanced remote procedures. Legal constraint: a Cayman-incorporated digital EMI or offshore EMI without an FCA licence or UK passporting rights cannot lawfully open a UK transactional account or provide payment services to UK-resident merchants; such offshore EMIs are not recognised as regulated institutions under the UK Electronic Money Regulations 2011 and would require full FCA authorisation or an appropriate equivalence/passporting arrangement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: UK tier-1 banks generally permit fully remote onboarding for UK-domiciled companies using digital identity verification. For an exempted Cayman company, banks almost always require at least one director or a properly authorised representative to attend either an in-person interview at the UK branch or a high-quality video due diligence call with certified ID and proof of address. Directorship physical presence is not universally mandatory but is a de facto requirement under enhanced due diligence where the parent entity is a Cayman tax-exempt vehicle; remote opening is available primarily through specialist fintech EMIs with higher transaction fees and stricter qualifying criteria.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cayman exempted company with no UK trading substance and no physical presence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered office address in Cayman, certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, register of directors and shareholders, audited or management accounts, a practical UK substance explanation, and a board resolution appointing the UK bank account signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Revenue-based financing for digital brands with cross-border royalty flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed financing agreements, underlying royalty or revenue-share contracts, detailed transaction flow diagrams, lender/borrower identity and existing bank statements, and a board-approved transfer pricing memo demonstrating arm's-length royalty rates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk counterparties or jurisdictions in the digital brand ecosystem
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced counterparty due diligence files, sanctions and adverse-media screening results, a defined customer acceptance policy, and documentary evidence of the commercial rationale for the payment chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected high transaction velocity through an account opened for a newly incorporated exempted company
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Projected monthly cash-flow statements, minuted treasury policy, a schedule of anticipated counterparties, and a signed compliance declaration confirming that funds will only be used for lawful revenue-based financing operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt status or preferential regime association
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Cayman tax exemption certificate, independent legal opinion on economic substance, confirmation of tax status in both Cayman and the UK, and a description of the operational activities to be conducted from the UK banking platform.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contributions from investors or group entities into the UK operational account must be routed as SWIFT MT103 wires or CHAPS denominated in GBP or USD, with precise remitter and beneficiary names, the UK account IBAN/BBAN, and an ISO 20022 transaction purpose code such as 'CFIN' (corporate finance) or 'INVS' (investment/securities). The bank will require the underlying capital subscription agreement, board resolutions approving the injection, source-of-funds evidence (investor net worth statements, audited accounts, or bank reference), and a Cayman certificate of incorporation; no UK exchange control approval is required, but the funds must be described as equity subscription, shareholder loan, or subordinated loan to allow classification under anti-money laundering and financial sanctions screening. If the capital is injected in USD, the beneficiary bank converts to GBP internally at the spot rate, or optionally the company maintains a USD account to avoid forced conversion.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements to suppliers, digital brands, and counterparties may be executed via SWIFT MT103 cash wires for immediate settlement, commercial letters of credit via MT700/MT707 for underlying trade finance, and SEPA Credit Transfers for euro-denominated disbursements. UK domestic vendor payments can be cleared via Faster Payments or CHAPS; UK-based digital brand fundings are also practical over Direct Debit/ACH rails. All outbound payments must pass OFSI and HM Treasury sanctions screening, and the compliance team should retain invoices, revenue-share agreements, and settlement instructions to demonstrate that payments are for permissible royalty financing or operating expenses.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for illiquid or restricted currencies
FX Options (vanilla put/call) for hedging committed royalty/revenue exposures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Exempted Company) and annual government fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Cayman Islands General Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 January following the fee year; the return covers the preceding calendar year ending 31 December. Newly incorporated exempted companies are aligned to the next 31 January filing cycle unless the Registrar grants a prorated extension.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or late payment triggers statutory monetary penalties and escalating default charges; continued default results in loss of good standing and may lead to administrative strike-off from the register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department for International Tax Co-operation (DITC), Cayman Islands Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 calendar days after the end of the entity's financial year; for a 31 December year-end, due no later than 1 March of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit the ESN attracts a fixed initial penalty; continued non-filing can result in daily penalties and strike-off action.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Economic Substance Return (ES Return) — required only if the exempted company is tax resident in Cayman and carries on a relevant activity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department for International Tax Co-operation (DITC), Cayman Islands Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the end of the financial year; for a 31 December year-end, due by the following 31 December.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance with the economic substance regime may trigger monetary penalties, additional daily default penalties, and compulsory strike-off for serious or prolonged default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Register update and annual confirmation (if shareholding or UBO changes occur)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Cayman Islands General Registry, through the registered-office corporate services provider
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Update within 15 calendar days of any change in beneficial ownership; annual confirmation coincides with the 31 January annual return cycle.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain or update the Beneficial Ownership Register is a criminal offence and may result in fines, imprisonment, and administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No automatic audit threshold applies to Cayman exempted companies. An independent audit is required only if the entity is regulated by CIMA, qualifies as a mutual fund or private fund, is licensed under a Cayman financial services law, or is otherwise required by its Articles of Association or financing covenants.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No Cayman domestic GAAP is prescribed; use IFRS, US GAAP, or another acceptable comprehensive basis of accounting consistently. Financial statements need not be filed with the Registrar for an exempted company unless the entity is regulated or subject to fund filing requirements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The exempted company must keep a Beneficial Ownership Register at its registered office and provide any ownership changes to the registered-office corporate services provider within 15 days of the change. The register is not publicly available, but designated authorities may inspect it. At each annual return cycle, the directors or registered agent must confirm that the Register of Members and the UBO Register remain accurate and reflect all shareholding transfers.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Exempt from corporate income tax on foreign-sourced income; no tax holidays or preferential deductions

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No corporate income tax return; Annual Return filed via Cayman Islands Companies Registry online portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 6 months of incorporation anniversary date

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company details, directors, share capital, registered office
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Standard disclosure for exempted companies; no tax computation fields

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: CI$100 base fine plus CI$10 per day (max CI$1,000); risk of deregistration and director disqualification

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Not applicable; Cayman imposes no dividend withholding tax; no DTA relief required
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% for royalties and interest payments; no withholding tax imposed

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: N/A - No transfer pricing rules or documentation requirements in Cayman Islands
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) apply to financing and holding activities; requires adequate employees, premises, and core income-generating activities

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Late or non-submission of Annual Return with Registrar of Companies
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to CI$1,000 plus daily surcharges; potential company dissolution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal fines, disqualification from office, and civil restitution orders

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain adequate economic substance for royalty financing operations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties up to CI$100,000 or higher; possible license revocation and business prohibition
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability for penalties; potential criminal prosecution and imprisonment

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion or aggressive tax structuring
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misrepresentation of income sources or failure to report taxable events under Cayman law
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties including fines and imprisonment; possible forfeiture of assets
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal liability, restitution, and travel bans

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company or lack of economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating without genuine business activities or substance requirements
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines and potential deregistration; administrative penalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal fines and disqualification from directorships

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to comply with anti-money laundering requirements for royalty financing fund
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Heavy fines, criminal prosecution, and license revocation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability including imprisonment for serious breaches
